form_b_example.lesson_title: Letter Z Handwriting and Spelling Lesson

major_sections.standards: Example: CCSS.ELA-LITERACY.L.K.1.A - Print many upper- and lowercase letters
major_sections.objectives: Students will correctly form uppercase Z and lowercase z using proper stroke sequence and connect the /z/ sound to the letter z
major_sections.materials: Sound cards, zebra cards, handwriting lines, pencils, Sound-Letter Hunt worksheet

review_connect.explanation: [The purpose of this part of the lesson is to start with a quick review of previously learned sounds. Do not use sounds that have not been directly taught. Do not use words that have sounds that have not been directly taught.]
review_connect.adaptation: *Adaptation1: Let me know if you would like activity examples, modifications of activities based on child ability level (low, middle, high), or additional modeling.

model_explain_engage.explanation: [The purpose of this part of the lesson is to connect a sound or sound patterns that you focused on during your reading block to writing its corresponding grapheme patterns. First, make sure children clearly can distinguish the targeted sound; then, hook that sound to the letter patterns through modeling and explaining the sequence of strokes for letters and correct order of letters.]
model_explain_engage.teacher_script:
#Teacher Script:
We've been working on the /z/ sound.
My turn. Listen to my sound /z/.
Put your hand on your vocal box–now say the sound /z/.
Did you feel your vocal box? (Children should respond yes)
That means you are using your voice, so we use our voice to make the /z/ sound.
model_explain_engage.gesture: +Gesture: Move hand in a zigzag motion through the air while making the /z/ sound
model_explain_engage.sequence_verbal_cues: ##Sequence Verbal Cues for letter z: Little line across. Slant down the stairs. Little line across.
model_explain_engage.adaptation: *Adaptation2: Let me know if you would like activity examples, modifications of activities based on child ability level (low, middle, high), or additional modeling.

guided_practice.explanation: [The purpose is to give children practice writing the letter while supporting proper pencil grip and correct sequence of stroke formation using handwriting lines.]
guided_practice.teacher_script:
#Teacher Script:
Let's practice how to write uppercase letter z first. We are not using our pencils yet. Let's do our Magic Finger Write +Level= Low. Place your finger at the top of the line. Let me see {teacher checks students finger placement}
guided_practice.adaptation: *Adaptation3: Let me know if you would like activity examples, modifications of activities based on child ability level (low, middle, high), or additional modeling.

application.explanation: [The purpose of this part of the lesson is to facilitate children's spelling of the letter or letter patterns when they hear the sound(s). This supports children's early coordination of matching sound to letter(s) for the purpose of spelling words.]
application.teacher_script:
#Teacher Script:
Boys and girls, I am going back to the /z/ Sound Hunt game, but now it's the Sound-Letter Hunt game +Level:Middle. I am going to say a word. You are listening to the beginning sound of that word.
application.adaptation: *Adaptation4: Let me know if you would like activity examples, modifications of activities based on child ability level (low, middle, high), or additional modeling.

wrap_up.explanation: [The purpose of this part of the lesson is to remind students what they were focused on and provide praise for their accomplishments]
wrap_up.teacher_script:
#Teacher Script:
Alright, boys and girls I am so proud of you. What sound have we been working on? {Teacher holds up zebra sound card] (Children respond /z/).
Perfect! And which of these letters say /z/ {Teacher provides children with a choice} (Children can touch the correct letter)
Show me how to write it (children air write with sequence verbal cues–e.g., little line across, slant down the stairs, little line across)
Wonderful! Kiss your brains.

form_f_example.title: Sequence Verbal Cues for Letter Formation

letter_z.uppercase: Little line across. Slant down the stairs. Little line across.
letter_z.lowercase: Little line across. Slant down the stairs. Little line across.

letter_a.uppercase: Slant down. Slant down. Little line across.
letter_a.lowercase: Around and up. Straight line down.

letter_m.uppercase: Straight line down. Straight line down. Slant down. Slant down.
letter_m.lowercase: Straight line down. Over the hill. Over the hill.

z_sound.gesture: Move hand in a zigzag motion through the air while making the /z/ sound

m_sound.gesture: Rub stomach in circular motion while saying /m/

s_sound.gesture: Move finger in snake-like motion while hissing /s/

form_h_example.title: Adaptations and Modifications by Ability Level

sound_sparks_game.low: Teacher points to sounds one at a time, gives extra wait time, provides individual support
sound_sparks_game.high: Faster pace, multiple sounds in sequence, student leaders

magic_finger_write.low: Teacher guides child's finger, slower pace, repeat multiple times
magic_finger_write.middle: Independent finger tracing with verbal cues
magic_finger_write.high: Air writing without visual support, eyes closed challenge

trace_and_say.low: Hand-over-hand support, larger dotted lines, fewer repetitions
trace_and_say.middle: Standard dotted line practice with monitoring
trace_and_say.high: Smaller lines, independent practice, peer teaching

low_level: Sensory letter formation in sand or rice
Large motor movements for letter shapes

required_components: Sequence verbal cues for letter formation
Sequence verbal cues for letter formation

letter_formation.4_mastery: Forms letter correctly with proper stroke sequence independently
letter_formation.3_proficient: Forms letter correctly with minimal prompting
letter_formation.2_developing: Forms letter with some errors, needs guidance

sound_recognition.4_mastery: Identifies target sound in all positions independently
sound_recognition.3_proficient: Identifies target sound with minimal prompting
sound_recognition.1_beginning: Requires direct instruction for sound identification
